html:
The world wars were the two global conflicts of 1914 to 1918 and 1939 to 1945, fought between alliances of the great powers on every continent. The chart treats them as one era of about thirty years, with the 1918 influenza pandemic between them.

World War I began in the Balkans and turned into years of trench war in Europe. It killed soldiers by the millions. Four empires fell between 1917 and 1922:

  • the Russian Empire, in the Russian Revolution of 1917
  • the German Empire and Austria-Hungary, in 1918
  • the Ottoman Empire, ended in 1922

The influenza that spread in 1918 and 1919 killed more people than the war itself. India alone lost millions in the 1918 outbreak.

World War II was larger still. Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler conquered most of Europe and murdered six million Jews in the Holocaust. Japan fought across China, Southeast Asia and the Pacific. The Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin bore the heaviest losses of any country. The war ended in 1945 after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

The wars left the United States and the Soviet Union as the two great powers and began the Cold War. They also broke the European colonial order. Britain and France came out exhausted, colonial troops had fought for them, and within thirty years most of Asia and Africa was independent in the wave of decolonisation.
